# c302 muscle channels (OpenWorm c302 0.12.1, MIT)

Five NMODL files as generated by jNeuroML 0.14.0 (org.neuroml.export) from c302's `parameters_C2`
network `c302_C2_Full.net.nml` when c302 was run as published on backhouse (5 Nov 2026,
`docs/worm/research/c302_port.md`): the body-wall muscle cell `GenericMuscleCell`.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `Leak.mod` | leak, 0.002 mS/cm2, erev -20 mV |
| `k_slow_muscle.mod` | slow K (one gate n), 0.458 mS/cm2, erev -30 mV |
| `k_fast_muscle.mod` | fast K (gates p^4 q), 0.0427 mS/cm2, erev -30 mV |
| `ca_boyle_muscle.mod` | Ca (gates e^2 f, Ca-dependent inactivation h), 0.813 mS/cm2, erev 0 mV |
| `CaPoolMuscle.mod` | fixed-factor Ca pool, decay 60.8 ms |

The channel set follows Boyle and Cohen 2008 (Biosystems 94:170, "Caenorhabditis elegans body wall muscles are
simple actuators"); the values are c302's published C2 fit. `src/wormemu/brain.py` inserts them into the 95
body-wall muscles when the `muscle_active` toggle is on and sets every value from the ledger (`c302_*` rows).
**One change, numerical only** (`mod/`; the files exactly as generated are in `generated/`). jNeuroML writes each
gate as `x_q' = rate_x_q` with the rate computed in `rates()`, so NEURON's cnexp integrates it as a forward-Euler
step. The Ca activation gate e has a 0.1 ms time constant, so at the brain's 0.5 ms step the unchanged file
diverges to NaN within 3 ms. In `k_slow_muscle.mod` (n), `k_fast_muscle.mod` (p, q) and `ca_boyle_muscle.mod`
(e, f) each gate now reads `x_q' = (x_inf - x_q) / x_tau`, which is the same equation (the generated rate is
`(x_inf - x_q) / x_tau`) and which cnexp integrates exactly. Each changed line is marked `wormemu:`. Check
(BRAIN_PORT.md section 6, M2, `data/worm/brain_runs/muscle_m2/`): one isolated muscle, steps of 0 to 30 pA, the
patched files at 0.5 ms against the generated ones at 0.025 ms: the same -10 mV crossings in every step, largest
voltage difference 0.42 mV (during the onset overshoot of the 3 pA step), plateau means equal within 0.002 mV.
